text: Harbour City erzielte zwei frühe Tore durch Elias Okafor und Marek Barros, der auch Spieler des Spiels wurde mit 9,8 Bewertung und 2 Vorlagen [#905] [#975]. Doch danach drückte Seabrook Town mit ihrer offensiveren 3-4-3-Formation und schoss 22 Mal aufs Tor, mehr als doppelt so viele wie Harbour City. Trotz Unterzahl nach der Roten Karte für Joon Whitfield [#870], erzielte Seabrook vier Tore. Besonders spannend: Kian Romano traf in der Nachspielzeit doppelt, beide Chancen hatten eine hohe Trefferwahrscheinlichkeit, also echte Top-Chancen [#1882] [#1906]. Die Taktikwechsel – Seabrook presste mehr und spielte direkter – brachten ihnen den letzten Punch, während Harbour Citys Ballbesitz und Passspiel zum Ende hin nicht mehr reichten [#1361] [#1884]. Ein wirklich aufregendes Spiel mit zwei Seiten: geduldiges Aufbauspiel gegen schnelle, offensivere Spielweise, das Seabrook am Ende gewann.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in de

- Seabrook Town won the match 4-2 against Harbour City despite conceding two early goals. [#905, #975]
- Kian Romano scored two late goals in added time (90+2' and 90+3'), both with high xG values of 0.605 and 0.952. [#1882, #1906]
- Marek Barros (Harbour City) was the player of the match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, and a 9.8 rating. [Player of the match data]
- Seabrook Town outshot Harbour City 22 to 10 and had a higher xG of 3.44 compared to Harbour City's 1.03. [team_stats]
- A red card to Joon Whitfield disrupted Harbour City before halftime, with the score at 0-0. [#870, #871]

- Harbour City operated with a 4-2-3-1 formation favoring patient short passing, aiming to build attacks through controlled possession and multiple passes, as shown by their 17-pass buildup leading to their first goal at 45' [#904, #905]. This reflects their intention to retain possession and create chances through careful ball progression rather than direct or fast transitions.

- Seabrook Town utilized a 3-4-3 formation with a focus on wide, crossing play and more direct attacking, evident in their higher possession (53.4%) and greater number of shots (22) and box touches (60). Their goals often came from quick regains and direct play, such as the goal by Tariq Marlowe at 53' arising from a single-pass regain and shot within 1 second [#1103, #1104], and their late goals following rapid build-ups involving only a few passes [#1881, #1882].

- The red card shown to Harbour City's Joon Whitfield at 43' (with the score 0-0) likely disrupted their defensive shape and allowed Seabrook to press more effectively, intensifying the pressure on Harbour’s midfield and defense and facilitating Seabrook’s more direct and higher pressing style after the 65' tactical adjustment [#871, #870, #1361].

- At 65', Seabrook Town increased pressing intensity and directness, playing with a higher defensive line to chase the game. This tactical shift resulted in a more aggressive style that produced three second-half goals (69', 90+2', 90+3'), exploiting spaces behind Harbour City’s increasingly stretched defense as they pressed higher and attempted more direct play late in the match [#1361, #1447, #1448, #1881, #1882, #1905, #1906].

- Harbour City’s initial style of patient ball circulation was compromised after being reduced to 10 men and trailing, forcing a late tactical change to press higher and play more direct themselves in the final minutes (90+2'), which coincided with conceding two quick goals, reflecting the risks of a compressed tactical shift when chasing the game [#1884, #1881, #1882, #1905, #1906].

In summary, Harbour City’s controlled, short-passing 4-2-3-1 was effective early on, but the red card and Seabrook Town’s 3-4-3 wide, crossing, and direct playing style combined with increased pressing and line height overwhelmed Harbour’s shape and facilitated Seabrook’s late comeback and eventual win.
